curation.lead:
Robert Kraft is the founder, chairman and chief executive of The Kraft Group, whose disclosed businesses include the New England Patriots, New England Revolution, Gillette Stadium, paper and packaging companies, and a portfolio of private-equity investments [SEC:0001193125-20-225055]. He joined the board of Apollo Global Management in May 2014 and resigned effective April 6, 2021 [SEC:0000950142-14-001006][SEC:0000950142-21-001237].

The Epstein-related evidence is a narrow 2019 attempted counsel-referral sequence [Finding #13181]. It documents Jeffrey Epstein's effort to refer a lawyer and later counsel-related activity involving Brad Karp, but it does not prove that Kraft retained the proposed lawyer, that Epstein or Karp caused any engagement, that Paul Weiss represented Kraft, or that Kraft communicated directly with Epstein [Finding #13181].

sections.title: Business and Apollo Board Role
sections.content:
A 2020 Apollo Global Management proxy identifies Kraft as founder, chairman and chief executive of The Kraft Group and lists holdings spanning professional sports, stadium and real-estate operations, paper and packaging businesses, and more than 100 private-equity investments [SEC:0001193125-20-225055]. Apollo appointed Kraft as an independent director in May 2014 and initially named him to its Conflicts Committee [SEC:0000950142-14-001006].

Kraft resigned from the Apollo board effective April 6, 2021 [SEC:0000950142-21-001237]. These filings establish a corporate-governance relationship with Apollo; they do not by themselves establish a relationship with Jeffrey Epstein or knowledge of Leon Black's personal advisers [SEC:0000950142-14-001006][SEC:0000950142-21-001237].

sections.title: The February 2019 Referral Sequence
sections.content:
On February 22, 2019, attorney Jack Goldberger alerted Jeffrey Epstein to Kraft's arrest, and Epstein replied that he was trying to have Kraft hire Goldberger [Finding #13181]. At nearly the same time, Epstein told Brad Karp to let him know if Kraft needed a local Palm Beach representative; Karp answered only that Kraft would need “the best there is” [Finding #13181]. The response did not accept the offer or name a lawyer [Finding #13181].

A later iMessage export labels a participant only as “Jack” and records that Kraft wanted him and his Quinn Emanuel lawyer to handle the matter [Finding #13181]. By March 4, Karp told Epstein that he had spoken with Kraft's Quinn Emanuel lawyer, and Epstein replied that “jack is very tied in” [Finding #13181]. The messages document later counsel-related activity, but the export does not preserve a unique selector identifying “Jack,” and the records do not establish who caused Kraft to retain whom [Finding #13181].

sections.title: Neighboring 2019 Legal Threads
sections.content:
The broader February–March 2019 message set also contains a separate urgent request for a lawyer for former Citigroup executive John Havens, a request for a civil attorney, Brad Karp's statement that he had ideas, and Karp's separate statement that he used Nardello for certain matters [Finding #13102]. Those neighboring messages show that Jeffrey Epstein and Karp discussed multiple legal or investigative referrals during the period, but the cited record does not assign every line to Kraft [Finding #13102].

This separation matters because the Kraft sequence proves an attempted Goldberger referral and later Quinn Emanuel contact, while the Havens, civil-attorney and Nardello lines concern distinct or unspecified matters [Finding #13181][Finding #13102]. It does not support describing Karp as coordinating Kraft's defense team or Nardello as working for Kraft [Finding #13181][Finding #13102].

sections.title: Evidentiary Boundaries
sections.content:
The verified sequence involves messages among Jeffrey Epstein, Jack Goldberger, Brad Karp and an iMessage participant labeled “Jack”; it contains no message authored by Kraft to Epstein [Finding #13181]. It also contains no engagement letter, invoice or matter-opening record identifying Paul Weiss as Kraft's counsel [Finding #13181].

The supported formulation is therefore limited: Epstein attempted to refer counsel, a later participant reported Kraft's interest in two lawyers, and Karp later spoke with Kraft's Quinn Emanuel lawyer [Finding #13181]. The records leave unresolved whether Goldberger was the exported “Jack,” how Kraft selected counsel, whether Epstein's offer to Karp was accepted, and whether Karp's later contact reflected a formal mandate, an informal referral or another role [Finding #13181].

curation.system_role: Robert Kraft appears in the verified Epstein-adjacent record as the subject of an attempted legal referral and subsequent lawyer-to-lawyer contact, not as a demonstrated direct correspondent with Epstein [Finding #13181]. His separate Apollo board service supplies corporate context but does not establish knowledge of or participation in Leon Black's personal advisory relationship [SEC:0000950142-14-001006][SEC:0000950142-21-001237].
open_questions: Can the iMessage participant labeled Jack be resolved through a unique selector or independent primary record?
Did Kraft retain Goldberger, Quinn Emanuel, or both, and if so, what records identify how and when each contact began?
In what capacity did Karp speak with Kraft's Quinn Emanuel lawyer, and was any Paul Weiss matter opened?
Did Kraft communicate directly with Epstein in any released or independently obtained record outside the cited sequence?
Which neighboring February–March 2019 messages concern Kraft, Havens or other distinct matters?

citation_findings.summary: Same-day February 2019 records show Epstein told Jack Goldberger he was trying to have Robert Kraft hire him and then offered Karp a local Palm Beach representative; Karp replied only that Kraft would need “the best.” A separate iMessage participant labeled “Jack” later reported that Kraft wanted him and a Quinn Emanuel lawyer, and Karp later spoke with Kraft’s Quinn Emanuel lawyer. Counsel engagement followed, but the records do not show Karp accepting Epstein’s offer, identify the iMessage participant by a unique selector, prove Karp caused the engagement, or show Paul Weiss represented Kraft.
citation_findings.detail: At 1:03 p.m. Goldberger emailed Epstein about Kraft’s arrest; Epstein replied at 1:04 p.m. that he was trying to have Kraft hire Goldberger. At 1:04 p.m. Epstein separately offered Karp a local Palm Beach representative; at 1:15 p.m. Karp said Kraft would need the best, without accepting or naming counsel. The iMessage export labels the later participant only as “Jack”; it does not preserve a unique phone or email selector for that participant. By March 4 Karp told Epstein he had spoken with Kraft’s Quinn Emanuel lawyer, and Epstein replied that “jack is very tied in.” This establishes a real follow-through sequence while leaving Karp’s causal role and any Paul Weiss mandate unresolved.
